articles.title: In Last Night’s Midterms, the Left Proved It Can Win
articles.author: Branko Marcetic
articles.content_excerpt: The Left has been so conditioned in the Trump era to look aghast and horrified at election results that it is still hard to fully believe the outcome today. Yet the historic events of last night really did happen: Donald Trump and Republicans suffered a historic rebuke from voters, handing Democrats wins up and down the ballot all across the country, flipping both chambers of Congress in their favor, and handing them the largest congressional majorities they’ve had since Barack Obama’s election. In many ways, the result is simple. articles.title: Reform Candidate Says UFCW Rep Tailed Him for 300 Miles to Thwart Petition Effort
articles.author: Lisa Xu
articles.content_excerpt: In a union that has been headed by one family with no competitive elections since 1984, a group of grocery workers is organizing for change. But this week, they say, union staff who back the incumbent administration went to outrageous lengths in an attempt to make sure there’s no election this year either. On Monday afternoon, Eric Marcuz, a veteran Northern California Safeway worker, stopped at the union office to pick up blank petitions to get on the ballot in the union’s upcoming election. Marcuz is running for president on the At What Cost slate in the 23,000-member United Food and Commercial Workers (UFCW) Local 8-Golden State, one of the largest locals in the union. articles.title: UAW Statement on John Deere Plans to Close Two Plants in Iowa
articles.author: Justin Mayhugh
articles.content_excerpt: The UAW is disgusted by John Deere’s latest attack on the working class of Iowa. The UAW will use every tool at our disposal, from our contract negotiations in 2027, to legislative and executive action, to keep good jobs in Iowa and stop the one-sided class war waged by John Deere. We are done seeing the massive profits our labor generates given away to Wall Street and our jobs being destroyed so some executive can make an extra buck. It’s time for America to come together to save John Deere from its own corporate greed, and fight back in the war on America’s factory workers.

What is at stake is the historical meaning of democracy itself: whether a republic founded upon the promise of popular sovereignty can survive the concentration of executive power, the systematic weakening of institutional restraints, the mobilization of political resentment, and the transformation of public life into an arena of permanent ideological warfare. articles.title: The 1956 Hungarian Uprising Was a Working-Class Revolt
articles.author: Adam Fabry
articles.content_excerpt: On October 23, 1956, tens of thousands of Hungarians took to the streets of Budapest. What began as a demonstration led largely by students rapidly became a popular uprising against the country’s Stalinist government. Within days, the authority of the Hungarian Communist Party had crumbled, Soviet troops had been forced to withdraw, and workers across the country were establishing their own councils to organize production and exercise political power. The Soviet leadership called it a “counterrevolution,” while Western governments celebrated it as a “revolt against communism.” Both interpretations obscured something fundamental: the Hungarian Revolution was driven by workers and ordinary people who wanted to free themselves from a system that claimed to represent their interests. articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Before we’re buried in hot takes on what the midterms mean, here is what we know: no one can afford anything. The mandate of this election is that costs have to come down and wages have to go up. articles.author: Ben Burgis

articles.author: Corey Robin
articles.content_excerpt: If there’s one person who saw yesterday’s repudiation of the right coming long before everyone else did, it’s Zohran Mamdani. In one way or another, he and the movement that created him are the architects of the Democrats’ victory. Two years ago, the day after the 2024 election, the mood was grim; the future was bleak. He spoke to white, black, brown, Muslim, Asian, but above all working-class men and women and, above all, in the Bronx and Queens. articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. In January, park rangers removed 34 interpretive panels from a slavery exhibit at Independence National Historical Park in Philadelphia. The signs, which described the lives of the nine people George Washington enslaved at the presidential residence there, were unceremoniously taken down — in some cases leaving the dried glue in place — to comply with President Donald Trump’s Executive Order 14253 , titled “Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History.” The order calls for the removal of signs that “inappropriately disparage Americans past or living” from the country’s national parks. articles.title: Giving Community Photos a Second Life
articles.author: Tiqua Jackson
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. A neighborhood organization may have years of photographs and still struggle to find a suitable picture for its next announcement. A street-fair photo is too small for print, a workshop picture has harsh lighting, and another carries last year's event date. For groups that run on volunteer time and limited budgets, taking new photographs for every newsletter or campaign is rarely practical. Thoughtful editing can make existing material useful again.
